features.headline: Which NHL players scored the most points in a single season?
features.desc: Connor McDavid looks to join Wayne Gretzky with a 200-point season.
body: Wayne Gretzky is the king of many NHL records. With points scored, Gretzky holds eight of the top 10 spots for most in a single season. He's also the only player to score 200 points in a season. Could Connor McDavid be the one to finally join him?

The Edmonton Oilers star started off the 2026-27 NHL season on a tear, finishing October at a 222-point pace. Gretzky's best year in points came in 1985-86, when he notched 215 from 52 goals and 163 assists.
Here's a look at other seasons that join The Great One's legendary campaign.

features.headline: 2026-27 MLB free agency, trade grades: Offseason analysis
features.desc: We've got you covered with grades and analysis on every winter signing and big offseason trade.
body: The 2026-27 MLB offseason is officially here, and we have you covered with grades and analysis for every major signing and trade as this winter — which is expected to include a labor stoppage — unfolds.
Whether it's a franchise-changing free agent signing or an unexpected blockbuster trade, we'll weigh in with what it all means for next season and beyond.

ESPN MLB experts Bradford Doolittle and David Schoenfield will evaluate each move as it happens, so follow along here, as this story will continue to be updated. Check back in for all the most recent analysis.
The deals: David Bednar accepts one-year, $23.15 million qualifying offer; Jonathan Loáisiga agrees to two-year, $18 million deal Grade: C+
Let's combine these two moves into one overall grade as the Yankees piece together the back end of their bullpen — a pen that ranked second in the majors with a 3.13 ERA in 2026.
The Yankees shoved Bednar into a corner by giving him a qualifying offer, which promised to limit his demand in free agency since he would have been tied to draft pick compensation.
By accepting it, Bednar's salary is now the highest average salary for a reliever, topping Edwin Diaz's $23 million with the Dodgers.

Other than a blip in 2024, Bednar has been steady since 2021, first with the Pirates and then with the Yankees after coming over at the trade deadline in 2025, posting sub-3.00 ERAs in five of his six seasons, including 2.47 ERA in 2026 when he racked up 35 saves in 39 opportunities.
He throws a four-seamer, splitter and curveball, with his splitter his big out pitch, holding batters to a.149 average in 2026 and.175 in 2025, with just one home run over the two seasons.

features.headline: Fred VanVleet's 'fresh slate' is driving Houston's early season success
features.desc: A healthy Fred VanVleet is commanding the surging Rockets after an ACL injury derailed his 2025-26 season. Here's why he's so important.
body: FRED VANVLEET BOILED inside watching the Houston Rockets "floating," he'd later say, as the Utah Jazz transformed a 12-point deficit into a 10-point lead over a span of 7 minutes, 39 seconds of a game he knew "was there for the taking."
"He was pissed off," Rockets coach Ime Udoka said, "and kind of went off on everybody."

VanVleet also unleashed that fury on the Jazz, who eventually fell 125-118 on Nov. 13 in an NBA Cup matchup, as VanVleet racked up 10 of his 17 points in the third quarter, catalyzing a 15-2 Rockets run heading into the final period.
Alperen Sengun jokingly revealed a new nickname for the point guard after the game: "Admiral."

VanVleet, 32, is navigating his NBA career now with more purpose, after acknowledging he had taken it for granted. It's a realization VanVleet came to while sitting out a 2025-26 campaign that teemed with expectations after Kevin Durant's arrival.
The point guard sustained a torn ACL at a workout in the Bahamas before training camp, leaving the Rockets without a veteran floor leader and bound for a second straight first-round postseason exit.

But the undersized, self-made veteran is steering the ship again in Houston. VanVleet is transforming the Rockets into contenders in the Western Conference, sitting at 12-4 and one game out of the 1-seed.

The Rockets rank 10th in assist-to-turnover ratio and 14th in turnover percentage after finishing 27th in both categories last season. VanVleet ranks fifth in the NBA in assist-to-turnover ratio (5.07) among players logging at least 25 minutes per game.

features.headline: MLB free agency tracker: 2026-27 offseason trades, moves
features.desc: We've got you covered on all the major MLB hot stove signings and trades.
body: The 2026-27 MLB hot stove was lit just days after the Milwaukee Brewers hoisted the franchise's first World Series championship trophy.

All eyes this winter are on the free agency of two-time Cy Young winner Tarik Skubal. But he's not the only one who will make a splash in the market, with Freddy Peralta, Randy Arozarena, Seiya Suzuki and Michael King among the other free agents to watch.
Which teams will go big to contend for the 2027 World Series title? And who will make the trades and signings that have everyone buzzing?
Below is a running list of notable transactions and updates from throughout the MLB offseason.
The New York Yankees and right-hander Jonathan Loaisiga are in agreement on a two-year deal with a club option for 2029, sources told ESPN, reuniting the reliever and club after a season apart.

The Colorado Rockies are acquiring right-handers Davis Martin and Luis Castillo in a trade with the Chicago White Sox, sources tell ESPN. The White Sox are getting LHP Sean Sullivan and catching prospect Douglas Veliz in return.
Right-hander Randy Dobnak and the Kansas City Royals are in agreement on a one-year, $1.35 million contract, a source tells ESPN.
Right-hander Sonny Gray and the Minnesota Twins are in agreement on a two-year, the team announced. The contract is for $55 million and includes an opt-out after the first season, sources tell ESPN.
The Boston Red Sox are acquiring catcher Nick Fortes in a deal with the Tampa Bay Rays, sources tell ESPN.

The Seattle Mariners are acquiring Gold Glove third baseman Maikel Garcia in a six-player trade with the Kansas City Royals, sources tell ESPN. The Royals are receiving three major league pitchers in return, headlined by right-hander Bryce Miller.

features.headline: Mauricio Pochettino's Man United squad audit: Should Fernandes, Rashford stay?
features.desc: New Manchester United manager Mauricio Pochettino inherits a squad built by his six predecessors. Which players have a future at the club, and which should go?
body: Mauricio Pochettino has arrived at Manchester United and the former United States men's national team coach has no time to waste as the new manager of the Premier League's fallen giants.

Pochettino's immediate task is to halt the team's slump and drag United out of the relegation zone, starting with Sunday's trip to Liverpool as his first game in charge. Securing a first league win since August is also a priority for the former Tottenham Hotspur and Chelsea boss.
However, the 54-year-old must look beyond the short term at Old Trafford. He must begin to shape a team in his own image, with players capable of playing the Pochettino way.

- Man United, Pochettino's to-do list based on what's gone wrong - Pochettino can't fix United on his own. The owners have to do their jobs - Where are they now? Every Utd player, coach, exec since Glazers' takeover

Former United captain Gary Neville said last week that, while interviewing him at Spurs in 2014, Pochettino was sat in front of a whiteboard with two lists of players: those he could trust and build around, and those he decided he could not work with.

Having inherited a squad built by United's six previous managers dating back to Louis van Gaal's signing of Luke Shaw in 2014, Pochettino must quickly assess his players and draw up a similar list of who will stay and who will go.
So with the Pochettino era about to start at United, what will his whiteboard look like at the end of the season? Who stays, and who has to go?
